alex (infra): Heads up — seeing p95/p99 latency SLO misses in eu-west-1 since ~10:12 UTC. Dashboards show a long tail when GPU util >90% and queue depth spikes. Feels like continuous batching pressure + max-batch constraints.

maria (mlops): ugh ok. Any specific models or pools?

alex (infra): Mostly text-gen-v2 on pool-eu-1. Metrics: batch_fill_rate down to 0.35, avg_batch_size 4 (max_batch_size=16), inflight_queue ~120. p99 at ~1.2s.

sanjay (runtime): Can you paste the model runtime config?

alex (infra): here are the relevant parts:
```yaml
model_policy:
  max_batch_size: 16
  max_wait_ms: 25
  admission_queue_limit: 200
  prefer_fill_over_latency: true
```

jess (sre): oncall-bot shows autoscaler triggered twice but new nodes didn't join fast enough (cloud region constraints). region eu-west-1 had node provisioning delay ~90s.

oncall-bot: autoscaler: requested +2 gpus to pool-eu-1 at 10:13:04, provision delay 87s, capacity applied 10:14:31.

maria (mlops): Sounds like a snowball: when util climbs, runtime tries to keep filling big batches (prefer_fill_over_latency), so requests wait for batch to fill up to 16, blocking others. But since arrival rate is bursty, fill_rate low -> many small batches and queueing.

sanjay (runtime): Agreed. Two levers: reduce max_wait_ms to favor latency, or lower prefer_fill flag / reduce max_batch_size. We can also enable small-batch fast-path for short sequences.

ajex (infra): typo ^^ alex: I can try a quick config change on a canary host. Propose:
```yaml
model_policy:
  max_batch_size: 8
  max_wait_ms: 8
  admission_queue_limit: 120
  prefer_fill_over_latency: false
```

jess (sre): +1 to canary. Also throttle burst admission at the router: lower per-pool concurrency so we don't overload GPUs while scaling. That buys time during node provisioning.

maria (mlops): Also we should look at sequence length distribution. If median length is short, prefer_fill is harming latency for little gain.

sanjay (runtime): I'll roll the canary to 2 hosts in pool-eu-1 now. Rolling command: `redwoodctl rollout --pool pool-eu-1 --config-file /tmp/canary.yaml --hosts 2`

oncall-bot: rollout job started (id=r12345) by sanjay at 10:15:12

alex (infra): After canary applied: p95 improved ~200ms, p99 down ~400ms on those hosts. Queue depth on canary workers dropped to ~20.

jess (sre): Nice. But global pool still noisy until autoscaler finishes. We should prevent repeated oscillation — set a short cooldown on prefer_fill toggle.

maria (mlops): Agreed. Follow-up: run a quick eval on our core prompt set to ensure quality not degraded with smaller batches. I can spin that up.

sanjay (runtime): Also adding a temporary admission cap at the gateway: `max_inflight_per_model=500` -> reduce to 350 for pool-eu-1 to slow new requests during scale. That'll reduce queue churn.

alex (infra): Sounds good. Cost note: increasing permanent capacity in eu-west-1 is expensive with current commitments. We'd prefer config + admission fixes first before capacity commit.

jess (sre): If canary holds and autoscaler finishes, let's revert prefer_fill and test increasing max_batch_size incrementally in low-traffic window. We'll document the trade-offs.

maria (mlops): Filing a short postmortem with graphs and the config diffs. I'll include the eval results and recommended default for text-gen-v2 in eu pools.

alex (infra): TL;DR — root cause: continuous batching pressure + prefer_fill + region provisioning lag. Mitigation: canary config (smaller batches, lower wait), gateway admission cap, run evals, hold off on immediate capacity buys.

sanjay (runtime): I'll keep monitoring p95/p99 and host queues; ping me if it drifts back up.

jess (sre): thanks everyone — great quick coordinated response. :thumbsup:
